title: Diff-ZsVQA: Zero-shot Visual Question Answering with Frozen Large Language Models Using Diffusion Model
abstract: Visual Question Answering (VQA) methods leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) aim to enhance performance in few/zero-shot scenarios. While the results attained by these approaches were outstanding, there remains scope for further enhancement. Given the remarkable capabilities demonstrated by Diffusion Models (DMs), we recognize that the DMs can potentially improve the performance of VQA by optimizing the generation of captions. Furthermore, existing approaches for prompt construction neglect the influence of non-original questions and generated question-answer (QA) pairs, which leads to adverse effects on the inference. This paper proposes a novel framework called Diffused Zero-shot VQA, shortly Diff-ZsVQA, which innovatively incorporates a powerful DM into the LLM-based VQA pipeline for image-to-text converting. Moreover, to reduce the impact of non-original questions and generated QA pairs, we devise an Original-Question-Centric (OQC) prompt whose examples’ questions are identical while contexts are diverse. We first construct initial prompts to formulate answer candidates, then the final answer is selected among options in answer heuristics via OQC prompting. Compared with previous LLM-based VQA methods, the proposed architecture is simpler and it brings a higher efficiency to predictions in zero-shot VQA. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Diff-ZsVQA with OQC prompt achieves competitive performance with higher inference speed than most existing methods.

title: Chapter 5 - Introduction of advanced generative AI models: diffusion and transformers
abstract: This chapter introduces advanced generative AI models—focusing on both Diffusion Models and Transformers—that underpin today's cutting-edge systems such as ChatGPT and StableDiffusion. We begin by presenting the fundamental concepts and methodologies behind Diffusion Models, including discrete-time frameworks like DDPM and DDIM, as well as score matching and flow matching techniques. Advanced topics, including diffusion models for text generation and latent diffusion models, are also discussed. The chapter then delves into the principles of Transformers, providing comprehensive guidance on building Large Language Models (LLMs) and applying these models across a variety of NLP tasks. Finally, we examine the current limitations of Transformer-based models and survey emerging research directions aimed at overcoming these challenges and pushing the boundaries of generative AI.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Driven Multimodal Medical Foundation Model for Unified Understanding, Reasoning and Generation
abstract: Purpose/Objective(s) To develop and validate a unified multimodal medical foundation model that combines visual understanding, cross-modal generation (image-text translation), and interpretable reasoning with visual grounding, and to quantify the gains enabled by multi-objective reinforcement learning (RL). Materials/Methods A discrete-diffusion Multimodal Large Language Model (dMLLM) was developed that represents both medical images and text as sequences of discrete tokens and generates outputs by parallel denoising. The model was pretrained on large-scale multimodal corpora covering understanding tasks (e.g., VQA/diagnosis) and generation tasks (e.g., radiology report generation and text-to-image synthesis). Unified optimization was performed using RL with a composite reward: (1) a cycle-consistency reward enforcing bidirectional coarse-grained alignment via image-to-report-to-image and report-to-image-to-report reconstruction; and (2) a multimodal inpainting reward enforcing fine-grained alignment by randomly masking 15–30% of image or text tokens and rewarding reconstruction conditioned on the complementary modality. For interpretability, a medical reasoning dataset was constructed by augmenting curated multimodal examples with chain-of-thought rationales and spatial annotations. Evaluation spanned report generation and report-to-image generation using standard quantitative metrics and expert review of reasoning and grounding quality. Results The proposed model improved report generation over a representative baseline from BLEU-1 0.256 to 0.416 (+0.160; +62.5%) and ROUGE-L 0.244 to 0.366 (+0.122; +50.0%) on IU X-Ray dataset, as shown in Table 1 of Supporting Document. For text-to-image synthesis, FID decreased from 1.66 to 1.594 (−0.066; 4.0% reduction). Grounded chain-of-thought produced spatially anchored explanations suitable for quantitative assessment and clinician review. Conclusion This work indicates the potential for a single RL-optimized medical foundation model to deliver high-performing and interpretable multimodal AI. Performance gains were observed across both recognition (report generation) and generative (text-to-image) tasks through RL-based cross-modal alignment, while visual grounding enabled transparent, spatially verifiable reasoning.

title: Denoising diffusion bridge for cross-modal alignment in three-dimensional scene understanding
abstract: Safe navigation, planning, and interaction in real-world environments are important engineering applications of artificial intelligence, motivating the use of large language models (LLMs) for geometric reasoning over three-dimensional (3D) scenes. Unlike two-dimensional images, 3D environments encode rich spatial structure, making accurate geometric reasoning essential for tasks like question answering, planning, navigation, and human-aligned interaction. Current approaches rely on shallow, single-step projections to map 3D features into LLM prompts-methods that struggle to fully bridge the nonlinear gap between structured geometry and the linguistic priors of frozen LLMs, particularly for compositional spatial reasoning. We propose a diffusion-based refinement framework for bridging 3D geometry and text prompts compatible with frozen large language models (DiffBridge3D), which explicitly models and corrects the misalignment between structured geometry and language priors. Specifically, we formulate this misalignment as structured noise in the prompt space. We further introduce a Conditional Diffusion Bridge that progressively denoises tokens derived from 3D features into prompts aligned with the effective text-prompt distribution of the frozen LLMs. The framework is trained end-to-end using answer-optimized targets selected from a per-sample prompt bank, without modifying the frozen LLMs. Experimental results on five 3D vision-language benchmarks demonstrate that DiffBridge3D consistently outperforms existing methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/junhui661/DiffBridge3D.
